_source: Collected 2026-10-06 via Splunk MCP from the test environment (identity_lookup_expanded, asset_lookup_by_str, aws:cloudtrail, Authentication data model, Windows process events) for the detection window. Facts are phrased in English for Jev.

web_admin: identity: service account, IT department, on the watchlist, priority high
cloud API calls came from 4 different public IP addresses
one of those IPs launched instances in 15 regions using a generic Linux scripting client
the account also created a new IAM user and a new access key, and deleted an access key
splunk_access: identity: service account for cloud data collection, on the watchlist
all calls came from one fixed IP address with the usual collection client
bstoll: identity: regular employee in the IT department, not a default, shared, or vendor account
this user's own workstation BSTOLL-L shows hidden, base64 encoded PowerShell launchers, a sign the workstation may be compromised
5.101.40.81: authentication outcome: every attempt failed or was blocked; no successful login from this source
167.114.13.150: authentication outcome: every attempt failed or was blocked; no successful login from this source
192.168.9.50: asset: not in the asset inventory
traffic outcome: every connection was blocked by the firewall; destinations include a public DNS resolver
FYODOR-L.froth.ly: asset: engineering workstation in the inventory
PowerShell command lines include hidden windows and base64 encoded commands, and code loaded from a registry value
BSTOLL-L.froth.ly: asset: not in the asset inventory
PowerShell command lines use a hidden, no-profile, base64 encoded launcher (-nop -sta -w 1 -enc)
ABUNGST-L.froth.ly: asset: not in the asset inventory
PowerShell command lines use a hidden, no-profile, base64 encoded launcher (-nop -sta -w 1 -enc)
BGIST-L.froth.ly: asset: not in the asset inventory
PowerShell command lines show no encoded or hidden commands
BudStoll: identity: regular employee in the IT department (same person as AWS user bstoll)

CreateDefaultVpc: actor: web_admin, from the same IP that launched 576 instances in 15 regions
AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress: actor: bstoll (regular employee, IT) through the AWS web console
the actor's own workstation BSTOLL-L shows hidden, base64 encoded PowerShell launchers, a sign the workstation may be compromised
RevokeSecurityGroupIngress: actor: bstoll (regular employee, IT) through the AWS web console
the actor's own workstation BSTOLL-L shows hidden, base64 encoded PowerShell launchers, a sign the workstation may be compromised
UpdateSecurityGroupRuleDescriptionsIngre: actor: bstoll (regular employee, IT) through the AWS web console
the actor's own workstation BSTOLL-L shows hidden, base64 encoded PowerShell launchers, a sign the workstation may be compromised
